turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi, yes I just came in today because I've been a bit concerned about some breathing difficulties over the last few days. It all started out with like a cough over the last week, but now I'm having trouble breathing as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh OK, well I'm sorry to hear that. So you said a cough as well, so the cough at least a week back and the shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, when did that start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So yeah, the cough, I usually have a cough. I've had COPD for a long time, but this past week the coughing has been much worse with a lot of more sputum and. Other than that, it started I would say two to three days ago. The cough got worse and then every time I'm moving around I like have to sit down and catch my breath, which is pretty abnormal for me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, so alright. So let's focus on the cough first. You said it's a wet cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I am producing a lot of sputum.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, what color is your sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's mainly like clear white.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah so you don't see yellow pus or anything green or bloody in there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so. But there's definitely like a lot more than what I usually produce.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, umm this cough, does it sound harsh, barky or does it sound muffled?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say it's a bit harsh at times. I wouldn't say it's barky or muffled. I do find myself wheezing a little over the last few days as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you find you have any chest pain associated with the shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, I don't really have any pains.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you ever experienced anything like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I did a couple of years ago, I had to be admitted because I had some shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But that was, I think, two years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And when you were admitted two years ago, did they tell you what you had?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, they said I had some kind of lung infection at that time, so they gave me some antibiotics while I was in the hospital.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, did they ever say to you that you had anything else like asthma, COPD, any longstanding conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah so I've had COPD for more than... I guess more than 10 years now so I think it just got a lot worse with the infection.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah alright. So this time around, have you had any fevers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've been having a couple of chills but like they would come and go. I didn't really think it was a fever.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any weight loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about changes in your hair or nails like or or skin like rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any changes in your vision or hearing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about smell or taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no. I think they're the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have a stuffy nose or runny nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do feel a bit stuffy, but it's not too bad.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any swelling in your in your legs or upper limbs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about calf pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No headaches.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Memory loss or confusion?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Changes in your bowel movement or abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Changes to urinating?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, that's all fine

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so besides the COPD, do you have any other longstanding conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do have some high blood pressure which I take, I think I take one of these medications called metoprolol.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when was the last time you had your blood pressure checked?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, probably like a month ago and it was pretty good. I've been checking by myself at home too and it hasn't been changing too much. I think the last one I took was probably like 135 / 80.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh, I see. OK, any hospitalizations besides the one that you had for COPD a year back?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, back when I was a kid I had my tonsils removed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you on any medications besides the metoprolol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do take multivitamins.I think that's yeah, that's about it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you take any puffers for your COPD?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so I do have three like different puffers I take. I can't remember the name. I do have some puffers I don't take. I've been using them right now. It has been helping with some of my shortness of breath, but I've definitely been having to use them way more than I used to.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you know which puffer you're on?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so I think one of them is called ventolin. OK, and then I think the second one is called the Spiriva.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sure, Yep.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So one of them should be a short acting beta agonist.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Just wanna make sure that you have one with a long acting and then the other one is a long acting beta agonist. OK, good. Alright, are you up to date with all your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And are you allergic to anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any family history of lung conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no I don't think so. Yeah, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. How about heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, my father died of a heart attack in his 60s.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, any cancers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My uncle had skin cancer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you know what type of skin cancer like melanoma, basal cell, squamous cell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think it wasn't the bad one. It was like the one they can remove right away.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh I see. OK, OK, that's good.Do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've been smoking for around, I would say the last 20 years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how much do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably I would say pack a day for the last 20 years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Umm, have you ever thought about quitting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I did. I did once and then went back onto it. I definitely do smoke less than before though. OK, but yeah, I don't think I'm ready to quit yet.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah no problem. Do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, yeah, maybe once a week I would have a small Cup of whiskey.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sure, that's fine. And any other drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no marijuana, no other drugs.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and where do you live right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Right now I live in a small bungalow in London.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any reasons to believe there are carpets, dust, mold, asbestos, anything that could be triggering your COPD?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, I don't think so. Everything is pretty up to date.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any contact with anyone that's been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been mostly trying to isolate and like just be in my own home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about travel to anywhere?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope, I've been in Ontario since the beginning of the pandemic.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah OK, that makes sense. Well, those were all the questions that I had for you today. Did you have any questions of your own?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I was just worried if it can be COVID or if it's just like another infection that I had like before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so we're definitely going to do a COVID swab on you and those results should take about 24 to 48 hours to come back to you. And in the meantime, because your symptoms do overlap with COVID, you should isolate for 14 days. Public health will be in touch with you if it's positive to do some contact tracing. If it's not COVID, it could be another viral infection that's been going around during this time of year which is likely because you have COPD, since you're already coughing more than you usually are and seeing more sputum. We will reassess to see whether your puffers are working. If we need to add any additional things like inhaled corticosteroids as well as antibiotics and so just keep an eye on your symptoms for now and will also want to do probably a chest X Ray and possibly a pulmonary function test. How does that sound?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah no problem.
